scope: Read-only feasibility and protocol parity audit; source inspection and retained provenance only. No model, provider, network, CI, Docker trial, quality scoring, frozen-code edit or commit.

verdict.summary: Native Harbor ClaudeCode/ZvecClaudeCode + Qwen is a materially different agent protocol from the 22 restricted custom rows and fits the user’s original Claude Code idea. Feasibility is supported statically; a separately frozen real-Docker fake-Anthropic infrastructure gate is required before a live pair.
verdict.interpretation: Reusing original q001 evaluates a new execution stack on a previously inspected task. It is neither held-out evidence nor a new QA task, and results must remain separate from the 22 custom rows and OpenCode phases. No expected improvement is asserted.

identities.prior_infrastructure_proof_scope: Accepted repair-v2 proof exercised native OpenCode configuration/installation. It proves package payload identity, not native Claude config loading, tool exposure, child accounting or Anthropic protocol.

findings.finding: Main registers Claude only with claude-opus-5, while Qwen3.8-Max is an OpenCode preset. resolve_agent_model rejects Claude/Qwen. Harbor itself passes the selected model unchanged when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set, and maps Opus/Sonnet/Haiku plus the subagent model to that same model.
findings.implication: A new explicit, frozen routing entry or thin invocation layer is necessary. Use qwen3.8-max with the existing Anthropic endpoint, not the custom-openai/ OpenCode identifier, and do not pretend the stock registry already supports it. Freeze credential mode and absence of unintended Bedrock/OAuth/fallback settings. Harbor reads ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL from host os.environ, whereas the API key uses _get_env; supplying only agent extra_env must not be assumed to activate the custom-base alias branch. Prove effective endpoint and all model aliases in the fake-provider trace.

findings.finding: The 22 custom rows expose exactly Read/Grep/Glob, plus one zg search tool for treatment. Native main does not set allowed_tools/disallowed_tools or max_turns; Harbor defaults to bypassPermissions and enables background tasks. Native CLI defaults therefore replace the former explicit restricted toolset; exact exposed tool names and actual child behavior remain unverified for this new route.
findings.implication: The change is a real agent-protocol test, not a rename or a repeat of the old harness. Native tool availability, permission resolution, child model aliases and child lifecycle require request-trace proof.

findings.finding: Custom runs disable all CLAUDE.md, auto-memory, slash commands and session persistence, use empty settings sources and strict MCP config. Native Harbor retains sessions, does not add those disables, may copy ~/.claude/skills, and supports optional skill/memory/MCP registration. Native zg installs into /logs/agent/sessions, the exact CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR Harbor uses.
findings.implication: Freeze fresh config/HOME/project state, optional registrations and environment sources. State isolation must cover both /root/.nvm and Claude’s separate /root/.local install cache volumes. No pre-existing skills or memory should silently enter a nominally fresh run.

findings.finding: Pinned Rust install_claude writes .claude.json, settings.json and global CLAUDE.md under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Its guidance includes retrieval routing, bounded-snippet reuse and stopping when evidence is sufficient. Custom runs disabled this guidance. The intended native guidance path is statically consistent; actual prompt inclusion has not been observed in this route. Harbor can overwrite .claude.json when mcp_servers is nonempty.
findings.implication: A fake-provider gate must show exact treatment guidance and MCP schema are loaded once, baseline has neither, and the configured zg server survives launch. Keep framework mcp_servers empty for this installation route, or explicitly prove an intentional merge; this is conditional overwrite risk, not an observed failure.

findings.finding: Both routes pin Claude 2.1.212 and high effort. All 22 historical rows used 900 s wall, 30 turns and per-request max output 8192. Only the later 16 rows additionally used a 24-tool/600-second admission hook; the first six did not. Main native Claude passes max_budget_usd=4.0, but no equivalent tool/turn/output cap in its runner branch. Optional ambient environment variables can supply some CLI limits.
findings.implication: Do not describe all 22 as having the 24-tool hook. Explicitly freeze the new route’s time/turn/output/effort settings and environment, separating inherited native controls from new controls. The client’s $4 budget is not a verified Qwen spending cap or billing measure. OpenCode temperature/thinking/output fields do not automatically transfer to Anthropic.

findings.finding: Harbor locates a primary directory excluding subagents, then parses only that directory’s top-level *.jsonl. It deduplicates streamed messages and sums those trajectory metrics. This establishes top-level trajectory scope, not complete root-plus-descendant accounting. Agent logs are retained/downloaded as a directory, so descendant raw files may still exist even though the parser omits them. No actual native-Claude child undercount has been demonstrated by this audit.
findings.implication: Native fixtures must create an actual linked child and retained child session evidence. A strict collector must reconcile root plus every linked descendant by session/message/request identity, distinguish unrelated background requests, and report completeness. Do not claim the existing OpenCode session-tree collector or the old child-disabled custom parser already proves this.

findings.finding: The native trajectory parser skips malformed JSONL lines, treats missing/null usage components as zero, and may return without a trajectory after conversion errors. The QA collector uses the last agent-step text and the default legacy-root usage scope; only the OpenCode branch requests collect_session_usage. Thus a nonempty answer and positive totals alone do not prove complete native Claude execution or accounting.
findings.implication: Require exact raw stream and recursive session inventory, a completed terminal result and tool/child states, finite complete usage components, identity reconciliation and an explicit Claude session-tree accounting scope. Missing/partial/malformed evidence must fail completeness rather than silently become zero usage. Measure evidence capture separately from solver/setup/outer wall time.

findings.classification: corrected inspection trace; not a defect
findings.finding: Claude.run merges stderr into the tee’d stream, but it calls exec_as_agent, which calls BaseInstalledAgent._exec. _exec prepends set -o pipefail and raises on nonzero exit. The initial hypothesis that tee inherently masks Claude status is therefore not supported by the full call chain.
findings.implication: Do not add an execution wrapper solely to repair nonexistent missing pipefail. Preserve merged-stream bytes honestly and validate nonzero exit/diagnostic retention with real-Docker negative fixtures. Do not label the merged file as separately captured stdout/stderr.

findings.finding: Native total_cost_usd comes from a CLI result event, not an independently verified provider bill. Qwen’s model pricing and budget behavior through this client are not established by the source. Native aliases/background/tool/guidance/state changes make the new route a bundle of protocol differences.
findings.implication: Record client-reported cost with its provenance but do not use it as audited Qwen dollars or claim causal attribution to one changed component. A fake provider proves transport/evidence plumbing, not production billing or native model quality.

required_before_live_gates.requirement: Freeze a separate native-Claude phase, exact upstream/Harbor/CLI hashes, q001 source/question/rubric, explicit route and endpoint/model/credential-name contract. Retain original phases unchanged; attempts=1 and retries=0 apply to the future pair, not hidden replacements. Do not reuse old native results.

Use actual Linux Docker and native Harbor ClaudeCode/ZvecClaudeCode with fake Anthropic SSE and fake embedding endpoints, no real provider credentials. Fresh containers/config/HOME/index and both setup/install cache volumes; hash original four Rust payloads and effective executable path before/after.

Trace native request bodies and init tool inventory. Prove qwen3.8-max root/child/alias routing, effective effort/output/turn settings, native tool behavior, treatment-only MCP registration plus exact installer guidance, baseline absence, no unexpected settings/skills/memory and no later MCP config overwrite.

Complete a deterministic native root -> actual linked child -> completed root fixture and real zg retrieval against frozen q001 source. Preserve full request logs and recursive session files; reconcile every root/child message ID, tool ID, usage component, cache component and final sentinel. Separate any unrelated background request and require unambiguous linkage, rather than inferring descendants from filenames alone.

Strict negatives: failed CLI exit with diagnostic text, malformed/truncated stream or session, absent usage component, missing descendant log, incomplete tool/child and timeout including leader exit with live descendant. Require invalid result/completeness status and whole-process-group plus container cleanup, with raw status/bytes retained. Inherited pipefail stays intact.

Freeze a Claude-specific complete accounting contract and independently verify its sums against fake-provider traces and persisted sessions. Preserve native trajectory as separate evidence; do not relabel legacy-root or opencode-session-tree-v1 as proven Claude accounting. Record setup/index, solver, raw native execution, evidence capture and outer-slot wall separately.

Retain a concrete reviewed proof archive with exact inputs/source/package hashes and honest network boundary. Fake endpoints with package installation network access are provider-offline, not air-gapped. Only after all gates pass, decide and freeze one fresh baseline/treatment q001 pair; no implied permission or claim of effect improvement follows from this report.

Resolve the explicit route and complete root/child evidence contract first. No live dispatch is justified by source parity alone.
